answer.generated: Parameter sharing in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) allows for efficient feature extraction across different locations in an image by applying the same set of parameters (weights) to multiple regions of the input image. This mechanism, known as local receptive fields, ensures that the same operation is performed at every spatial location, thus enabling the network to detect features regardless of their position within the image. By reusing the same parameters across various parts of the image, CNNs significantly reduce the number of parameters needed compared to fully connected layers, making the model more computationally efficient while still maintaining the ability to identify consistent features across different locations.
